status: Source-derived street positions plus original compressed layout (scripts/city_layout.py). Engine-integrated; geography is compressed, not surveyed.

source.note: The raw file is kept out of Git; only the derived positions below are recorded.

licence.name: Open Government Licence - Toronto
licence.attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Toronto.

method: Centreline segments were selected by street name and projected (EPSG:2952, metres).
Coordinates were rotated 16.6 degrees so the downtown street grid is axis-aligned (Yonge St runs about 72.9 degrees from east, Queen St about 16.1 degrees).
Origin: Yonge St at Queen St. u is metres east of Yonge, w is metres north of Queen.
Each street's position is the median rotated coordinate of its segments inside the downtown window; extents are the observed segment ranges, rounded.
observed_extents: Front St W runs Bathurst to Yonge; Front St E Yonge to about 2015 m east.
Ossington Ave runs Queen to Bloor and beyond.
University Ave runs Front to College, continuing as Queen's Park.
Harbord St runs Ossington to St George; Wellesley St from Queen's Park east past Parliament.
Carlton St runs Yonge to Parliament; Gerrard St E continues east across the Don.
King St E ends near the Don; Broadview Ave starts at Queen/Eastern.

compression.rule: Piecewise-linear: streets keep their real order and proportional spacing between anchors. North-south streets are snapped to 64 px where possible to keep the city atlas inside its tile budget; seam rows shared with the West and East scenes are unchanged.
omitted: Lake Shore Blvd (folded into Queens Quay)
simplified: Harbord St and Wellesley St form one continuous row (the Hoskin Ave jog is omitted).
College St, Carlton St and Gerrard St E form one row.
Front St continues east of Parliament as Mill St.
Don River bridges: Bloor (Prince Edward Viaduct), Gerrard, Dundas, Queen and the waterfront.
The rail corridor passes over Dufferin, Bathurst, Spadina, Yonge and Parliament.

neighbourhoods: Blocks take the character of the neighbourhood at their real position (REGIONS in scripts/create_city_art.py). Extents are approximate character areas, not official boundaries; City Neighbourhoods data is a reference only and no boundary geometry is bundled.
landmarks: City Hall and Nathan Phillips Square
Art Gallery of Ontario and Grange Park
Ontario Legislative Building and Queen's Park
landmark_art: Original pixel art placed at the landmark's compressed position; no photographs, logos or map imagery.

parks.note: Source facts below are what the art follows; sizes and positions are compressed game design, recorded separately.

sources.supports: Queen's Park Cres E/W, Queen's Park, Hoskin Ave and Wellesley St W geometry and the Queen's Park Trl network (same downloaded file as above).
The Legislative Building and the monuments in Queen's Park, including the King Edward VII equestrian statue in the park north of the building.
The historic gates at Trinity Bellwoods' main south entrance on Queen St W; the dog bowl.
The off-leash dog bowl in the centre of the park, at the bottom of a slope, south of Dundas St W.
Allan Gardens Conservatory: the glass-domed Palm House and its greenhouses.
The Grange (1817) at the south end of the AGO complex; the south half of the estate opened as Grange Park.

queens_park_m.frame: Rotated grid metres as above (u east of Yonge, w north of Queen).
queens_park_m.trails: Queen's Park Trl segments radiate from a circle near w 1590 in the northern section, with a ring path near the edge; the middle of the oval has no trails (the Legislative Building) and the south end has the front-lawn paths.

compressed_design.queens_park: The crescent is about 36 px wide at the core's compression; the game draws its arms 104 px apart (centrelines at x 460 and 564) so the park reads at street level. Harbord/Hoskin and Wellesley both meet it at the y=176 row; the arms leave College either side of the front lawn and rejoin at y=128 as Queen's Park, which runs to Bloor. 45-degree corners stand in for the curves. The Legislative Building spans the oval at y 208-240 with its front lawn and flagpoles to College; the statue is at (512,176) with six of the real spokes and old trees on the lawns. The ROM stays at Bloor and Queen's Park; Victoria College, University College and the Whitney Block are left as lawns and trees (tile budget).
compressed_design.trinity_bellwoods: Fills the block from Queen to Dundas between Ossington and Bathurst: gates at the south edge, the walk north, the dog bowl in the centre, trees. Wider than the real park relative to the compressed block.
compressed_design.allan_gardens: Fills the block between Yonge and Parliament, College/Carlton and Dundas: the Palm House dome and two greenhouse wings on a paved forecourt at the north, paths to Dundas and the south corners, trees.
compressed_design.grange_park: South of the AGO: The Grange as a small brick house at the north of the park, the walk to Queen and trees.

navigation.note: Names the HUD announces (content/places.json, scripts/create_places.py) and the district art they label. Source facts are listed per source; rectangles, building sizes and positions are compressed game design over the Centreline-derived street plan.

sources.supports: Harbord Village: bounded by Bloor St W, Spadina Ave, College St and Bathurst St. The art region formerly labelled The Annex (which lies north of Bloor, off this map) is renamed Harbord Village.

City neighbourhood Palmerston-Little Italy: Bloor St W, Bathurst St, College St and Dovercourt Rd. The art region formerly labelled Seaton Village (north of Bloor, off this map) is renamed Palmerston; Little Italy keeps College St.

Business improvement area names used for commercial districts: Financial District, Entertainment District, Discovery District, Chinatown, Kensington Market, Little Italy, West Queen West, Garden District, Downtown Yonge, Roncesvalles Village, Bloordale Village, The Junction, Bloor West Village, Broadview Danforth / Greektown on the Danforth, Riverside, Leslieville. BIA areas are not residential neighbourhood boundaries.
The Financial District's towers at King and Bay over the PATH network; Union Station reached through the PATH.
MaRS at 101 College St, the south-east corner of College St and University Ave: the 1913 Toronto General Hospital College Wing restored with a glass atrium and new tower.
The hospitals on University Ave north of Dundas (Toronto General, Mount Sinai, Princess Margaret, SickKids), known as Hospital Row.
Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, across Queen's Park from the Royal Ontario Museum, south of Bloor St, on Victoria University's grounds.
Convocation Hall (1907), the domed rotunda at 31 King's College Circle, south of Hoskin Ave and west of Queen's Park Crescent.
Roy Thomson Hall, 60 Simcoe St, the round glass concert hall on the south side of King St W at Simcoe St.
Royal Alexandra Theatre (260 King St W) and Princess of Wales Theatre (300 King St W), a block apart on the north side of King St W.
St James Cathedral at King St E and Church St, its tower and spire over the King St entrance; St James Park beside it.
City Council voted in December 2023 to rename Yonge-Dundas Square as Sankofa Square; the new name was unveiled in 2025.

compressed_design: Neighbourhood rectangles follow the art regions (real metres on the downtown grid, compressed with the street plan) or, outside downtown, the compressed road graphs. The HUD keeps a neighbourhood until the courier is 16 px outside it, so a boundary street does not flicker.

Junction names put the north-south street first and drop the suffix (SPADINA & DUNDAS); a pair longer than one HUD row uses PK or a slash; Parliament St at Queens Quay is too long and is not announced.

Landmarks are announced within 24 px of their footprint. Bay St, Simcoe St, Church St and Elizabeth St are not on this compressed map, so the Financial District towers, Roy Thomson Hall, St James Cathedral and the hospitals stand on the nearest drawn block.

The Financial District's towers are generic: black steel and glass towers with a low pavilion, gold glass towers by Union Station and a red granite tower with a notched crown. They are not labelled with company names.
